title: System Simplification
hook: The system I built was so complicated that even I stopped using it.
statement: Complexity kills execution. The simpler the system, the more likely it actually gets done.
explainer: Every extra step is another place to stall. A clever system you skip half the time loses to a simple one you run every single day.
sop: Write out your process or offer step by step, even the tiny steps.
Rate Simplicity and Consistency from 1 to 10.
Cut any step that doesn't directly serve the main outcome.
Run the trimmed version and check the core value still holds.
Re-audit every quarter. Complexity sneaks back in.
equation_example: Simplicity 8, Consistency 9. 8 × 9 = 72 out of 100. That's a system that's easy to run and actually gets run. Lower means complexity or inconsistency is capping what gets done.
question: Pick one process and write down what you could cut in half this quarter without losing the core value.
closing_statement: If it's too complex to follow, it won't get followed.
caption:
Principle Nº 143: System Simplification

The system I built was so complicated that even I stopped using it.

Complexity kills execution. The simpler the system, the more likely it actually gets done.

Your turn: Pick one process and write down what you could cut in half this quarter without losing the core value.
